{"version": 1, "content": "

MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 How this works

  1. Run one of the Image to 3D Model workflows first. It writes a .glb into ComfyUI/output/3d.
  2. On the Load 3D node press upload 3d model and pick that .glb. ComfyUI copies it into input/3d so the node can see it.
  3. Drag inside the 3D view to rotate to the angle you want, then press Run.

Flux Klein redraws that angle as a finished picture. Because it is always the same 3D model, every angle you render is the same object, which is what you cannot get by asking an image model for another view.

 Load Diffusion Model

Download flux-2-klein-9b-int8-convrot.safetensors9.4 GB 

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/flux2

 Load CLIP

Download qwen_3_8b_fp8mixed.safetensors8.06 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

 Load VAE

Download flux2-vae.safetensors320 MB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

 After placing the files, restart ComfyUI or refresh model lists using R shortcut.

{"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS FOR YOUR CARD

The same three models as workflow 5. The only thing to tune here is denoise, which has its own note next to the sampler.

 What it costs

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090
A render at 1024 x 1024about 3 seconds
The first run after starting ComfyUIabout 7 seconds longer
Memory in use at the busiest moment21.4 GB

That 21.4 GB is what ComfyUI chose to use when it had 24 GB free, not what the workflow needs. It packs down when there is less room, so a smaller card can still run this. It was only measured on the big card, so treat a small card as untested rather than ruled out.

 The sampler

Four steps at a CFG of 1 with euler and simple. Those are the turbo settings this model is built for and they do not need changing.

 If you run out of memory

  • Lower the width and height on the Load 3D node. That is the picture size here, and it is the biggest lever.
  • Close other programs using the graphics card, browsers included.
  • The 3D model's own file size barely matters. Only the photograph of it reaches the sampler.

{"version": 1, "content": "

KEEPING YOUR ANGLE

Whatever you set up in the 3D view is what you get: the angle you turned to, how close you zoomed, and where you dragged the object with the right mouse button. The picture is painted on top of your view instead of being composed from scratch, so an object pushed off to one side stays off to that side.

 Denoise

One setting does this, on the sampler. It is set to 0.70 and it decides how much freedom the model gets:

DenoiseWhat you get
0.50your view is kept, but the rough edges of the 3D mesh come back
0.70your view is kept and the surfaces come out clean
0.85it starts re-composing, so the object drifts and changes size
1.00your framing is ignored. That is workflow 5

Those were measured on the same 3D view with the same seed, so they compare. If the result looks too close to the raw 3D model, raise it a little. If the object starts moving around, lower it.

 Picture size

There is no size list here, on purpose. The picture comes out at the size of the photograph taken of your 3D view, and that is the width and height on the Load 3D node. Change those two numbers, then drag once inside the 3D view so it takes a fresh photograph at the new size.

 Which one to use

  • This one when the angle is the point: you posed the model and you want that exact shot, cleaned up.
  • Workflow 5 when you just want a good picture of the object and do not mind where it ends up. It composes the shot itself and it has the size list.
